title: The Critical Regularity Frontier
mathematical_role: Separate scaling-critical norms, conditional continuation criteria, partial regularity, and the unresolved universal smoothness-or-breakdown alternative.
learning_objective: See why established conditional and partial results do not collapse into a solution of the Clay problem.
literal_semantics: The velocity scaling u_lambda(x,t)=lambda u(lambda x,lambda^2 t) makes 2/q+3/p=1 the mixed-norm critical line.
Continuation criteria are conditional implications from finiteness of controlling norms.
Partial regularity constrains the possible singular set without proving it empty.
Universal three-dimensional smoothness or admissible breakdown remains open.
nonliteral_semantics: The ladder does not assert that any sufficient continuation condition holds for every smooth datum.
The visual ordering is logical pedagogy, not a proof implication from partial regularity to global regularity.

notes: Candidate semantics are bounded by the existing documentary source; no new mathematical source is admitted by this visual operation.

renderer.version_or_environment: Python 3 standard library; deterministic SVG generator v1
reproducibility_notes: The generator uses no network, randomness, timestamps, or external data.
Repository tests compare generator output byte-for-byte with the committed SVG candidate.

accessibility.alt_text: A status ladder separates the scaling-critical line, continuation criteria, partial regularity, and the open universal three-dimensional Navier-Stokes problem.
accessibility.long_description: The plate starts with the critical scaling relation, then gives an established conditional continuation row and an established partial-regularity row. The final dashed row is the still-open universal smoothness-or-breakdown alternative, explicitly separated from the proved statements.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: The plate accurately distinguishes critical scaling, conditional continuation, partial regularity, and the open parent problem.
not_claimed: Universal finiteness of a critical norm
